adoptionGates.currentResult: Implemented for UIKit and macOS 14+ AppKit with newest-only targetTimestamp external ticks; macOS 12-13 keep the absolute-deadline fallback. AppKit package-scoped diagnostics and FoveaAnimationMacLab now bind lifecycle, target-buffer, scheduler-control and refresh-observer behavior. W5_PT_144 prevents lifecycle time from regressing behind a future targetTimestamp; W5_PT_145-147 bind the automatic-deadline control, source-frame commit hook and observer-only display link, and W5_PT_148 binds the exact driver playback-start clock anchor. The fixed-six/no-retry physical-Mac lifecycle capture remains green. A later fixed-six-pair Release timing study samples both schedulers on the same NSView.displayLink.timestamp refresh coordinate and scores against the exact playback-start anchor. On one arm64 macOS 27 host, all six pairs have no-worse external start-anchored p95 error and no-worse source-frame skips; median anchored p95 is 14.102375 ms external versus 75.461355 ms deadline, with 0 versus 82 total skipped source frames. Actual median display-link interval is 16.666625 ms in every retained run even though maximumFramesPerSecond reports 120, so maximum-FPS-derived missed/early counts are supplemental only. This is a scoped internal Fovea scheduling result, not a cross-player or release ranking.
adoptionGates.boundary: FoveaAppKit keeps the macOS 12 deployment floor; the targetTimestamp path is macOS 14+ and the old deadline loop remains the 12-13 fallback. The physical-Mac A/B observes committed source-frame state at the same view-display-link timestamp and is anchored to the exact driver start clock, but it is not hardware pixel scanout timing. It covers one host and one synthetic 60-frame variable-delay timeline. The primary direction gate uses anchored p95 timing error plus raw source-frame skips; energy, thermal, memory, startup and maximum-FPS-derived missed/early counts are not part of that gate. No third-party, physical-iOS, cross-platform or global Pareto claim follows. Stable physical iOS and exact production ImageCraft integration remain required.
adoptionGates.nextEvidence: Collect physical-Mac energy/thermal in separate runs that do not add another concurrent display sampler; require non-inferiority before calling the local scheduler change Pareto-improving. When a stable physical iPhone is online, run the semantically equivalent W5 player set with the same source timeline and target-buffer diagnostics. Startup remains excluded until the exact published ImageCraft production adapter is pinned.

requires: lower peak bytes or decode churn
adoptionGates.currentResult: Implemented locally as a deterministic actual-byte learned cap: provider frames are validated against target geometry and the single-frame animation-memory budget before publication; after observing exact DecodedImage.estimatedByteCost, later windows are capped by cache capacity / maximum observed frame cost. Tight-budget publication prioritizes the current frame. Warning pressure advances publication generation so an already in-flight normal-size window cannot publish after the warning; the retry uses the warning-size window. Existing shared frames are not destructively trimmed per session.
adoptionGates.boundary: No targetPixels x 4 hard-budget assumption is used. The first uncached batch still uses the existing frame-count window because no trustworthy actual frame byte cost exists yet. Proactive warning trim remains deferred because AnimationFrameMemory is shared across independent view clocks; a safe implementation must union retention keys across all active drivers before deleting frames.
adoptionGates.nextEvidence: On physical iOS devices, compare equal animation-memory budgets against Gifu, FLAnimatedImage, YYImage-derived policy references and current fixed-window Fovea; require non-inferior missed-frame/recovery tails plus lower or equal decoded-byte churn before adding any predictive controller.

adoptionGates.currentResult: Default-off BenchmarkDiagnostics experiment implemented. Fovea computes gcd(all normalized frame durations, one second), requests an integer preferred FPS only when that exact-boundary cadence is below the attached screen maximum, and records the requested FPS in presentation diagnostics. Ordinary FoveaImageView playback remains maximum-refresh.
adoptionGates.boundary: W5_DEVICE_PT_002 is configuration evidence only until executed on a physical device. An independent display sampler must not be present in energy runs because it can alter ProMotion refresh behavior.
adoptionGates.nextEvidence: On a stable physical iPhone, compare maximum-refresh and timeline-aligned modes for 100/150/250 ms variable-delay timelines using the common W5 presentation oracle; collect energy in a separate run without an extra display-link sampler.

PT001/002 cover the real authorized FoveaSystemPipeline plus retained separate-default APNG first-frame and full three-frame timeline pixels. PT003 covers a retained two-frame zero-duration GIF, explicit 10 ms timing replacement and exact direct-ImageCraft pixels. PT004 deliberately supplies an invalid zero-duration replacement after a valid ImageCraft prepare; timeline normalization fails closed with invalidZeroDurationReplacement and no runtime driver is registered, exercising the adapter post-prepare failure cleanup branch. The production ImageCraft pin remains older; publication, exact pin adoption, explicit adopted animation-error mappings, broader corpora and physical iOS gates remain open.
